rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a blastocyst with large blastocoel, thinned zona, visible compact ICM, and generally cohesive TE. Minor overcall in calling it broadly AA from the image alone, and TE/ICM quality are somewhat harder to confirm precisely on this single frame.

Thoroughly integrates age, BMI, ovarian response, tubal factor, prior biochemical pregnancy, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, and transfer timing with embryo quality and prognosis, including the important hydrosalpinx caveat.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis and recommendations clearly tied to embryo morphology, patient age, diagnosis, and known limitations of morphology-only assessment.

Recommendations are well aligned with IVF practice standards: elective single embryo transfer in a good-prognosis 33-year-old, caution about hydrosalpinx, appropriate luteal support, and avoidance of unsupported add-ons.

Provides clear next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx review, luteal support, uterine evaluation if recurrent failure occurs, and nuanced discussion of when PGT-A may be considered.
